role_sought: Member of the European Parliament, head of the Tisza national list
result: Elected; Tisza second with 7 of Hungary's 21 seats
detail: First election contested by Tisza under Magyar, two months after he joined the party; it became the largest opposition force. He took up his seat in the EPP group.

role_sought: Member of the National Assembly for Budapest's 3rd constituency; head of the Tisza national list and candidate for prime minister
result: Elected; Tisza won 141 of 199 seats (two-thirds majority)
vote_share: Budapest 3rd constituency: 43,112 votes (63.67%); Tisza national list: 3,385,890 votes (53.18%)
opponent: Attila Steiner (Fidesz–KDNP), 20,248 votes (29.90%); nationally Fidesz–KDNP led by Viktor Orbán (38.61%, 52 seats)
detail: Turnout was about 79% (78.99% according to the final results), the highest since 1990, and Viktor Orbán conceded defeat on election night. The figures for Budapest 3 are the National Election Office's results at 100% processing.

election: Election of the Prime Minister by the National Assembly
vote_share: 140 votes in favour, 54 against, 1 abstention (100 required)
detail: Elected at the inaugural sitting of the new parliament and sworn in the same day, ending Viktor Orbán's 16 years in office.
